sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill for a house in the city of Peoria?
sections.html:
Peoria County bills it. A house inside the city limits of Peoria pays one bill that combines the city, the school district, the park district and other taxing bodies, and the Peoria County Treasurer, who is also the County Collector, sends and collects it. The City of Peoria sets its own rules for registration and transfer tax, but it does not mail the property tax bill.

The county page notes that taxes can be paid to the Treasurer, to participating banks or to township collectors, and it carves out the City of Peoria Township Collector as a separate place to pay. Ask which of those applies to your parcel before you send a check, because a payment made at the wrong counter has to be redirected.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Peoria, and how does that affect a sale?
sections.html:
Peoria is the Peoria County seat, on the Illinois River, and the principal city of a metro area of about 402,000 people. Europeans first settled the site in 1691, the town was incorporated in 1835 and the city in 1845. The 2020 census counted 113,150 residents, the eighth most of any city in Illinois, spread over 47.97 square miles of land.

Health care now leads the local economy. OSF HealthCare has been the largest employer since 2021, and the medical district sits around the junction of Interstate 74 and Knoxville Avenue next to downtown. Caterpillar moved its headquarters out in 2018, and manufacturing of machinery, metal products and chemicals remains important. Hospital and university jobs steady the rental and owner market in the neighborhoods nearest the bluffs and the medical district.

Winters bring cold and snow, with average snowfall of 26.3 inches a year per Wikipedia, and summers are hot and humid. That weather shows up in roof, gutter and furnace condition on older houses, which a buyer's inspector will check.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Peoria homes and owners?
sections.html:
QuickFacts estimates the city at 110,920 people in July 2025, a 2.0% drop from the 2020 base. Only 57.5% of homes are owner-occupied, compared with 67.0% across Peoria County, so landlords and tenants are a large part of any local sale. The median owner-occupied value for 2020-2024 is $156,200.

  • Median gross rent is $1,005 a month.
  • Median household income is $59,410, and 21.0% of residents are below the poverty line.
  • Median monthly owner costs are $1,525 with a mortgage and $647 without one.
  • The city has 49,037 households averaging 2.20 people.
  • Mean travel time to work is 17.9 minutes.

Those are citywide averages. A bluff-top house and a house near the river flats can sit far apart on value and tax bill.

sections.h2: What changed on the 2026 assessment for the City of Peoria Township?
sections.html:
The county's 2026 notice for City of Peoria Township gives a January 1, 2026 valuation date and a required level of 33.33% of market value. The county median level was 31.25%. Sales from 2023, 2024 and 2025 were used. The Supervisor of Assessments applied an equalization factor of 1.0700 to residential, commercial, industrial and farm home site classes alike.

The notice tells owners to call the township assessor first, at 427 W Main St, Peoria, IL 61606 or (309) 324-7459. A formal complaint to the Peoria County Board of Review was open from June 1 through September 30, 2026, and the notice says you must file one to preserve the right to appeal. That window has closed, and the next one opens June 1.

The notice also gives a way to test your own assessment: divide it by 33.33%. If the answer is higher than what the house would sell for, it may be over-assessed.

sections.h2: What are the Peoria property tax dates and penalties?
sections.html:
The county issues a single yearly bill and divides it in half. For 2025 taxes payable in 2026 the halves were due June 9 and September 9, 2026. Anything paid or postmarked from June 10 or September 10 onward carries a penalty of 1.5% per month or part of a month, and the county states there is no grace period.

sections.h2: What city rules touch a Peoria house sale?
sections.html:
Peoria's transfer tax is $2.50 for each $1,000 of value or fraction of $1,000 stated on the transfer declaration, under a 1989 ordinance. It is paid at the Peoria County recording office. If money changes hands on a commercial or multi-family property, the city also wants a zoning certificate dated within the past year, issued by Community Development at 419 Fulton, Room 300, (309) 494-8600.

The city runs a property registration program. Under its FAQ, a home must be registered if it is any of the following:

  • rented to a tenant, including a family member
  • vacant for six months or longer
  • an investment property, meaning not the deeded owner's residence
  • being sold on contract for deed until the deed transfers
  • a multi-family building
  • a short-term rental of 29 days or less
  • in foreclosure

Registration fees are waived for a few cases, including a vacant house listed for sale and a house in probate, though those still have to register. The FAQ shows 2023-2024 fees of $75 for a single-family home, $75 plus $20 per added unit for multi-family, $75 per short-term rental unit with an 8% room tax, and $300 per parcel every six months for foreclosure. Confirm the current amounts with the Office of Accounts Receivable at 419 Fulton Street, Room 100.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes on a Peoria house?
sections.html:
Peoria County sells unpaid taxes in early November. Buyers bid from 0% to 9% interest, and if nobody bids the county takes the parcel at 9% as trustee. Interest is added at the sale and every six months. The owner still holds title during redemption, which defaults to two years and can be stretched to three. For homes of one to six units the county gives a minimum of two and a half years.

Redemption goes to the Peoria County Clerk, 324 Main St, Room 101, in one payment of cash, a cashier's check or a money order. Title company and personal checks are not accepted. A seller in that position should order the Clerk's redemption estimate and share it with the closer.

sections.h2: Which exemptions apply to a Peoria homeowner?
sections.html: The county page lists an owner-occupied exemption of $6,000 off equalized assessed value, a senior exemption of $5,000, a returning veterans exemption of $5,000 and a disabled persons exemption of $2,000. Disabled veterans receive $2,500, $5,000 or a full exemption depending on the service-connected rating. The county's senior deferral program charges 3% and is repaid when the home is sold, so a seller who used it should expect a payoff at closing. Questions go to the Supervisor of Assessments at 309-672-6910.

faqs.q: Does the City of Peoria collect my property tax?
faqs.a: No. The Peoria County Treasurer sends and collects the bill, and taxes can also be paid at participating banks or at the township collector. The city handles registration of rentals, vacant and foreclosure properties and its own transfer tax.

faqs.q: What is the Peoria transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: The city's instruction sheet prints $2.50 for each $1,000 of value or fraction of $1,000 stated on the transfer declaration. It is paid at the Peoria County recording office, and commercial or multi-family transfers need a current zoning certificate.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a vacant house in Peoria?
faqs.a: Yes, if it has been vacant six months or longer. A vacant house listed for sale qualifies for the fee waiver but must still be registered, with proof of the listing. A house in probate gets the same treatment. Call the Office of Accounts Receivable at City Hall to register.

faqs.q: When is the Peoria appeal deadline for assessments?
faqs.a: For 2026 it was September 30, and it has passed. The Board of Review accepts complaints from June 1 until 30 days after the township publishes its changes. Speak with the City of Peoria Township assessor before you file.

faqs.q: How late can Peoria taxes be paid before the sale?
faqs.a: For 2025 taxes the Treasurer had to receive payment by 5 p.m. on November 6, 2026, and postmarks did not count. The sale was set for November 9, 2026. After a sale, taxes are redeemed through the County Clerk instead.
